summary: Instagram is carrying the channel: most Hindi videos get 1,000+ views there, while YouTube Shorts mostly gets under 50 views. The best videos are about robots and 'dumb-but-clever' sensors (gyro, clap switch, PIR, line follower), and they also earn the most likes, shares and saves. Everyday-object explainers (taps, doors, smoke alarms, touchscreens) and the one English video get little attention, and the newest posts have too little data to judge yet.
winningPattern: Hindi Instagram Reels about a robot or a sensor that seems to have a 'missing sense' or surprising limitation. Title is a bold, curious statement with a twist, such as 'X ke bina robot gir jaata', 'Taali nahi, sirf shor sunta hai' or 'Dimaag nahi hota'. The hook names the surprise in the first line and the video then explains the one core component simply. Robot/maker subjects beat household-appliance subjects, and the 🤖 or 👏 emoji with a short title works better than a generic '🤔 Kaise Pata Chalta Hai?' question.
doMore: Make robot and maker-project videos (gyro, line follower, IR, clap switch) the main series, since they win on both platforms
Write titles as a surprising claim ('X nahi hota, phir bhi...') instead of a plain 'Kaise kaam karta hai?' question
Post to Instagram first and treat it as the main platform; test on YouTube with a stronger first-second visual hook
Add a clear share or save prompt at the end, such as 'Dost ko bhejo jo robot banata hai', because shares and saves are the strongest signals
Turn the best performers into follow-ups, such as part 2 or a related component, and reuse their title shape
stopDoing: Stop making household-appliance explainers (taps, mall doors, lifts, smoke detectors) with the '🤔 Kaise...?' title format
Stop posting near-duplicate topics (two smoke detector videos, two IR sensor videos, two tap videos) in the same week
Stop English narration for now; the single English video did not reach Instagram and earned little
